summary: Iter-30 P3 refactor validated end-to-end. All 4 refactor targets behave identically to pre-refactor. BACKEND (12/12 new iter-30 tests + 14/14 iter-20 sequential re-run = 26/26 PASS, 1 skip for unseeded assessment course): (a) _build_digest_html split — POST /api/enterprise/organizations/digest/preview returns HTML that contains org name, KPI labels (Readiness/Certifications/Avg progress/Seats), the 1/25 seats string, <!DOCTYPE html>, ends with </html>, and meta {critical_signal_count,pending_patch_count,generated_at}; unauth → 401/403; non-member → 404; non-admin PREVIEW allowed (200) but SEND rejected (403); admin SEND returns log with id/org_id/recipients/delivery/sent_at/meta and no _id. (b) fulfill_seat_increment split — unauth→401/403, non-owner→403 (_resolve_org_for_user require_admin=True), owner+unknown session→404 with 'not found' detail (_load_seat_txn contract), pending Stripe txn returns 200 with fulfilled:false or 502 (get_checkout_status). (c) SANITY REGRESSION: /api/health=200, /api/admin/analytics?days=30 returns 30-bucket zero-filled signups_per_day + certs_per_day arrays, /api/admin/orgs $lookup returns orgs with seats_used field (verified newly-created org shows seats_used>=1). FRONTEND: /enterprise/portal loads for org owner (Iter30 UI Co org). MemberList orchestrator + 4 sub-components + useMemberActions hook: 1 member row visible pre-create; open-create-user opens CreateUserModal; submit-create-user creates user AND surfaces TempCredsModal with 14-char password; close-temp-creds dismisses; MembersTable then shows 2 rows with remove-member-{user_id} button visible ONLY on the non-owner row (owner has none — role-guard correct). InviteForm send-invite submission POSTs successfully and clears the email input on 200. SeatEditorModal + useSeatEditor hook: manage-seats opens seat-editor; typing 30 into seat-target triggers debounced preview (~200ms) — seat-preview element renders 'CHARGE SUMMARY — Adding 5 seats: $90.00/month starting now (prorated on renewal)' from the /seats/preview endpoint; apply-seat-change button enabled (seatTarget !== org.seat_count). Zero console errors during the flow.
critical_code_review_comments: digest_router.py:35-197 — Five-helper split is clean and each helper is self-contained. _load_digest_data cleanly separates the two DB reads (intelligence_cache + curriculum_patches). _kpi_row_html / _signal_card_html / _patches_section_html are pure string builders (no side-effects), which makes them trivially unit-testable in isolation without hitting the DB. _digest_shell_html correctly takes pre-rendered kpi_html + body_html + briefing_url so the shell is decoupled from KPI/body semantics. The orchestrator _build_digest_html reads clearly (4 lines of orchestration vs the previous 90-line monolith). One P2 nit: _kpi_cell and _esc live BELOW _digest_shell_html — Python allows this because they're called at runtime, but reading top-down the flow is now (helper → shell → orchestrator → private-utils) which is slightly unusual. Consider grouping utils (_esc, _kpi_cell) above the section builders. Non-blocking.

enterprise_router.py:446-593 — Four-helper split of fulfill_seat_increment is textbook. _load_seat_txn owns the 404+403 lookups (nice: raises HTTPException so caller stays flat). _verify_stripe_payment cleanly wraps the try/except for Stripe I/O and encapsulates the amount-mismatch → 409 check (defence-in-depth against session-metadata tampering, preserved from iter-29). _resolve_fulfill_target is a pure function (int, int) → int — perfect for unit test. _claim_and_apply_fulfillment atomically does find_one_and_update + org update + billing event + fire-and-forget activity log; returns None on concurrent-claim, otherwise the claimed doc — the caller uses this truthy/falsy return correctly on line 588. Idempotency invariants preserved. One code-review nit: _claim_and_apply_fulfillment has 7 parameters — could be reduced by packing (status_resp, paid_cents) into a small dataclass or by moving the Stripe response into txn['stripe_status_resp']. Non-blocking; the current signature is still readable.

MemberList.jsx (56 lines) — the orchestrator is now a pure composition of 4 sub-components + 1 hook. State ownership is correct: showCreateUser is a purely UI concern that stays here; the temp-creds and error state live in the hook (business logic) — good separation. Minor nit: MemberList.jsx does not memoize its callback into MembersTable — every render creates a new arrow closure for onRemove — but since MembersTable is not React.memo'd this doesn't actually matter. Non-blocking.

useMemberActions.js (73 lines) — invite / createUserDirect / removeMember all return a boolean 'ok' so the child forms can decide whether to reset (InviteForm) or close (CreateUserModal). Consistent contract. removeMember uses window.confirm — fine for now but consider migrating to a shadcn AlertDialog for consistency with the rest of the app. Non-blocking.

SeatEditorModal.jsx (84 lines) — presentational shell + hook. Note however that SeatEditorModal STILL owns 6 pieces of state (seatTarget/setSeatTarget/seatPreview/setSeatPreview/seatBusy/setSeatBusy) by lifting them into the parent (EnterprisePortal) via props. A cleaner P3 could have moved those into useSeatEditor entirely (hook owns state, modal owns just open/close). Current signature is still improvement over the monolith but has room for another pass. Non-blocking.

useSeatEditor.js:13-21 — the debounce useEffect depends on [seatTarget, open, setSeatPreview] but setSeatPreview is a React setter from the parent, whose identity is stable, so the effect will only re-run on real changes. Behavior verified in browser (200ms debounce). One subtle: on modal close (open=false), the effect returns early WITHOUT clearing an in-flight fetch's .then, so a late response after close could still call setSeatPreview on a modal that just re-opened. Practical impact: near-zero because the next open resets seatTarget to org.seat_count via the parent's onClick handler (EnterprisePortal.jsx:130). Non-blocking.

IterCorp .example.com domains work correctly through email_validator — the iter-20 tests that were previously failing on .test TLD now pass sequentially (14/14). The 8 'skipped' iter-20 tests reported earlier were an xdist LoadScopeScheduling artifact (module-level pytest.iter20_* state doesn't cross workers) — pre-existing, not related to iter-30.
